en: The Sūtra of the Secret Ritual of the Great and Swift Spiritual Efficacy of the Five Great Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattvas, in one fascicle;
translated by Vajrabodhi.
Relying upon what is taught in the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra*, I [compose this] for those bhikṣus of the final age who lack merit,
yet long maintain the secret words of the Buddhas; for those whose fortune and wisdom do not manifest,
who hold no office or rank, and who, though of noble lineage and high standing, have meager roots of merit.

To transform and deliver all sentient beings, this reveals the most secret dharma—the path of spiritual efficacy of the Buddhas of the three periods of time. It is the swift, profound, and ultimate dharma;
may the bhikṣus and others who uphold the legacy of the World-Honored One Śākyamuni bestow wealth and treasures according to their capacity.
For the sake of the fruit of Bodhi, it is called "Thin Offering"; one should carefully contemplate its transmission and practice it.
If one's giving does not reach the level of reverence, the response to practicing the Way will not be realized.
To manifest the great power of this dharma’s efficacy, one should first establish the secret mandala.
Using white sandalwood, cypress, or cassia— indeed,
sacred wood that has stood for a hundred years—
one constructs a circle using a celestial disk (*tianpan*).
The square is two and a half inches and another three inches;
the ground disk is four inches and another seven inches on each side.
Furthermore, the color of the sky is entirely blue.
The inner courtyard of the ground is yellow,
the middle courtyard is blue,
and the outer courtyard is red.
Below, the four sides are azure-green with yellow beneath;
the heavens are one cun and three fen thick,
and the earth is one cun thick.
Furthermore, divide it into eight parts.
On the eastern side of the celestial disk,
paint an image of the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja, the Treasury of Merit and Wisdom.
Seated upon a white jewel lotus flower,
wearing a jeweled crown of the five buddhas,
and with his body adorned by various kinds of necklaces and ornaments.
The right hand bestows fearlessness;
the left hand holds a precious lotus flower,
upon which is a *viśvavajra*.
The color of the form is yellow.
To the south is the syllable TRAḤ,
which transforms into the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, the Fulfilled One.
He sits upon a red lotus flower.
His crown is adorned with the five buddhas,
as previously described.
The form and color are red flesh;
the right hand holds a precious sword,
and the left grasps a blue lotus.
Upon the flower is a wish-fulfilling jewel (*cintāmaṇi*).
As the jewel revolves, flames emanate from it.
To the west is the syllable *hrīḥ*.
He transforms into the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha Bestower of Boons,
seated upon a purple lotus flower.
His jeweled crown and his adornments are as described previously.
With palms joined at the chest,
the form and color are like a red *pārijāta* flower;
in the north is the syllable *Aḥ*.
He transforms into the Bodhisattva Vimalagaganagañja,
seated upon a white lotus flower,
adorned with a jeweled crown as before and with all other ornaments as before.
The left hand bestows fearlessness;
the right hand holds a precious lotus flower.
Above is a moon disc,
its shape and color white like water;
in its center is the syllable *vaṃ*.
He transforms into the Bodhisattva Liberation Ākāśagarbha.
His jeweled crown is as described before, his adornments are as described before,
and he sits upon a yellowish-white lotus flower.
The right hand bestows fearlessness;
the left hand holds a precious lotus flower,
upon which rests a single-pronged vajra.
The color is yellow.
Next, on the summit of the celestial disk (tianpan), paint the image of the King of the Seven Stars.
Next, within the inner court of the terrestrial disk (dipan), paint the images of the eight deities in the eight directions.
The images of the Four Heavenly Kings at the four corners are as in the preceding examples.
The image of Śakra-devānām-indra in the east is as in the preceding example.
The image of Yama-rāja in the south is as in the preceding example.
The form of Brahmā in the western quarter is as illustrated.
The image of Vaiśravaṇa in the northern quarter is as illustrated.
Next, in the central court, the twenty-eight lunar mansions (*nakṣatras*) are to be painted.
In the east are seven men of greenish-blue color, wearing green garments, holding weapons;
in the south are seven men of red color, wearing red garments, holding weapons;
in the west are seven men of white color, wearing white garments, holding weapons.
In the north, there are seven male figures of black complexion clad in black robes, holding weapons. Beyond that,
in the outer enclosure, the thirty-six animals are depicted,
beginning with Jia and Yi.
The various classes of yakṣas seek him out;
his image is painted,
or his name, color, and form are depicted.
The corners and ears follow their respective directions.
The ground of the inner courtyard is yellow;
the ground of the middle courtyard is blue.
The ground of the outer courtyard is red;
know that it is painted with colors. 2.
Chapter on the Attainment of Siddhi: The Second Chapter on the Attainment of Siddhi by the Bodhisattva Mahā-ākāśagarbha. The Root Supreme Heart Dhāraṇī is as follows:
Namo ākaśe āgaccha | Oṃ arigamari hili svāhā. This is the mantra of the Bodhisattva of the eastern direction.
Oṃ vajra hūṃ. For those seeking official rank and a righteous livelihood, the mantra of the Bodhisattva of the South is:
Oṃ vajra nātra. For those seeking wealth, nobility, and wisdom, the mantra of the Bodhisattva of the West is: [Oṃ vajra nātra].
Oṃ Vajra Hrīḥ. For those who seek to achieve love and attraction, the mantra of the Bodhisattva of the North is: Oṃ Vajra Aḥ.
For those who seek liberation and the pacification of calamities, the mantra of the Bodhisattva of the Center is: Oṃ Vajra Aḥ.
Oṃ vajra vaṃ. For those who wish to fulfill all their aspirations, the mudrā is as described in the Yoga Sūtra.
The practitioner first establishes the maṇḍala through meditative union (*yoga*).
One may dwell wherever one finds pleasure, provided that one seeks out a secluded place.
One should remain far removed from clamor, filth, and impurity; do not associate with boys or girls, those lacking faith, novices, the destitute, or those clad in soiled garments.
Seeking accomplishment,
one should be thoroughly diligent and careful,
preparing and arranging the ritual implements.
Place the principal deity upon the offering tray.
Facing the superior direction, recite the root mantra one million times over three periods of day and night, as desired, until completion.
One will immediately attain great wisdom and achieve the supreme, ultimate bliss among humans.
If one desires to attain total mastery over all things, [one should practice this].
According to the direction, prepare the ritual implements and perform the homa;
all that is sought shall be fully accomplished.
[This concerns] the substances and so forth appropriate for the homa.
As it is said in the *Sarvaguṇasiddhipaṭala*, these secret arts may only be resolved through oral transmission from the master;
for in the final age (*paścimaka-yuga*), disciples will harbor a sense of negligence and contempt toward the Dharma,
and thus one must not grant them these teachings.
According to the *Fanbu buji* (The Miscellaneous Records), if anyone wishes to obtain great wisdom,
they should pray to the Bodhisattva of the South and to the Deva Vaiśravaṇa;
by so doing, they will certainly obtain it.
If a person wishes to obtain the great affection of a king,
they should pray to the Bodhisattva of the western direction, Vaiśravaṇa;
by doing so, they will certainly attain it.
If a person desires to obtain a queen, a concubine, or even a daughter of noble rank who is most beloved,
they shall surely obtain her by first performing prostrations before the Bodhisattva and praying to him.
If a person wishes to be cherished by high ministers and noble officials,
they should pray as previously described to the former Bodhisattva;
they will certainly obtain it.
If a person desires to obtain the status of a great and wealthy elder with urgency,
they shall surely attain it by praying to the Southern Bodhisattva, who is superior even to the heavens.
If a person desires to obtain a high official position or seeks refuge in those worthy of respect,
they will certainly attain it by invoking the Bodhisattva of the East as an adjunct to Śakra, the Lord of Devas.
If a person desires to surpass all others and attain sovereign power over the world,
they should empower Brahmā with the Bodhisattva of the North;
by praying to him, they will certainly achieve it.
If a person wishes to fulfill all their worldly and supramundane aspirations,
they should empower the eastern deity with the central bodhisattva; by so praying,
they will certainly attain them.
If a person wishes to manifest great spiritual efficacy for others,
they should empower the deities of the northwest with the Bodhisattvas of the south;
by praying thus, they will surely achieve it.
If a person desires to obtain great efficacy and benefit all sentient beings,
they should employ the Bodhisattva of the East to empower the deity of the Southwest;
by praying thus, they will surely achieve their aim.
If a person desires to obtain official rank, title, or emoluments,
they shall pray to the Bodhisattva of the East while invoking Vaiśravaṇa;
thus they will obtain them.
If a person wishes to be loved and cherished by all people,
they should pray to the deity above the Bodhisattva of the Western Quarter;
they will certainly obtain it.
If a person desires to achieve victory in debate,
they should invoke the Bodhisattva of the South to empower Brahmā;
by praying thus, they will certainly succeed.
If a person wishes to subdue wicked people,
they should empower the northern bodhisattva toward the southwest;
by praying thus, it will certainly come to pass.
If a person wishes to cure a fever,
they should invoke the Bodhisattva of the Central Direction to empower the deity of the Northwest;
by praying thus, the illness will certainly be eliminated.
If a person wishes to eliminate ailments such as phlegm disorders, swelling, skin sores, or abscesses,
they should invoke the Bodhisattva of the North and add the Deity of the Southwest; by doing so,
these conditions will certainly be removed.
If a person wishes to remove obstacles and difficulties regarding their official rank,
they should invoke the Bodhisattva of the East to empower the deity of the northwest; by doing so,
they will surely attain their goal.
If a person wishes to become a sovereign king among all Dharma masters,
they shall surely achieve it by invoking the Bodhisattvas of the south and adding the deities of the southeast.
If a person wishes to obtain the protective mindfulness of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
they will certainly attain it by adding the Bodhisattva of the Central Direction to those mentioned above and offering prayers.
If a person desires to be loved and cherished by wealthy people,
they will certainly obtain this by invoking the southern Bodhisattva, Vaiśravaṇa.
If a person wishes to bind the celestial foxes and terrestrial foxes,
they should pray by invoking the Bodhisattva of the East toward the southwest.
If a person wishes to eliminate all afflictions caused by possession by ghosts or spirits,
they should invoke the Northern Bodhisattva, adding the deity Yama,
and pray to them.
If a person wishes to eliminate the fixed karma of all beings,
they should pray to the deity above the Bodhisattva of the East.
If a person wishes to eliminate the short lifespans and premature deaths of children,
they should pray to the deity above the Bodhisattva of the East.
If a person desires that all women give birth quickly and without difficulty,
they should pray to the deity above the Bodhisattva of the North.
If a person wishes to bring to rest all evil spirits who are afflicted by evil poisons and delusions,
they should pray to the Eastern Bodhisattva, the one who adds grace to the heavens.
If a person wishes to counteract the curses of wicked people,
they should invoke the Bodhisattva of the North upon the deity of the Southwest;
by praying thus, they will surely succeed.
If a person wishes to bring an end to the calamity of all fires,
they should invoke the Bodhisattva of the Central Direction to empower the deity of the Northwest Direction and offer prayers to him.
If a person wishes to eliminate the calamity of drought-demons,
they should invoke the Central Direction Bodhisattva while adding Indra as a witness and offer prayers.
If a person wishes to eliminate the calamity of a prevailing epidemic,
they should invoke the Bodhisattva of the North together with the god Yama.
If a person wishes to attain rebirth in the Ultimate Bliss Land in the highest grade of the highest birth,
they should pray to the Bodhisattvas of the West and the deity Yama.

If a person wishes to deliver their parents of seven generations, their six types of relatives, and all sentient beings from the extreme suffering of the hells, so that they may be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss,
they should take the Bodhisattvas of the Western Quarter as their witnesses and invoke Brahmā.
Pray thus: if a person desires that husband and wife may love one another,
they should employ the Bodhisattva of the Western Quarter together with the Deva Vaiśravaṇa.
Write the names of the man and woman together, place them within a container representing heaven and earth, seal it,
and offer prayers.
If a person wishes to cause a husband and wife to separate from each other or bring about evil between them, [they should do so].
One should pray by invoking the Bodhisattva of the North to add his power to the deity of the Southwest.
If a person wishes for their husband and wife to be separated from each other as they were originally, yet continue to cherish one another with love, [they should perform this rite].
One should pray by invoking Vaiśravaṇa, the Heavenly King of the Western Quarter, through the empowerment of the Bodhisattvas.
If a person desires to obtain all manner of wealth, yet it is stolen or lost, they shall regain it.
By invoking the Bodhisattva of the North together with Yama,
one will certainly obtain what is desired.
If a person wishes to recover those who have gone astray, including cattle and horses that have fled, [they shall be recovered].
By adding the Bodhisattva of the South to Brahmā, one shall obtain [the desired result] through prayer; these constitute the forty items of the aforementioned secret arts.
The ritual procedure for consecrating *sugandha-madhu* (honey) is detailed [below].
The ritual for seeking the power of hearing and retaining [the Dharma] is as described; seek it and you shall know it.
These teachings were transmitted from India by Dharmadeva at the site of Bodhi.
His ritual implements were not numerous;
people of the time all called them "efficacious methods.
He empowered the offering substances using the mudrā and mantra of Hayagrīva.
Oṃ amṛtodana bā hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. The seal of the Great Wheel Maṇḍala: Form fists with both hands;
hook the earth and wind fingers respectively and place them at the heart.
Recite the mantra three times while rotating [the rosary]. Next, consecrate the altar. Next, enter it into one’s own mouth with the mudrā.
The mantra is: Oṃ vajra-karaja hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ. The mantra for consecrating the rosary is: Oṃ vairocana māle svāhā. Next, recite the mantra for rotating the rosary:

Oṃ vajrayakṣiye jāpamaye hūṃ. This is the minor mantra of Śrīdevī. Oṃ mahāciliye svāhā. This is the mantra of the Heavenly King in Brahmī script. Oṃ vicisutaka-sicce svāhā. This is the general mantra of the Four Heavenly Kings. Oṃ jambhalasudhāraśe svāhā. This is the mantra of the Messenger. Oṃ dhu lu dhu lu dhiri dhiri dhuru dhuru kathaye svāhā. This is the mantra of the Great Samaya Seal. Regarding the mudrā: form two vajra-fists with the backs joined together.
Place the two index fingers together at the crown of the head;
with this mudrā, move it from the heart to the crown three times, raising it each time.
Immediately, scatter it above [the head].

*Namo samanta buddhānāṃ dharmadhātu sarvabhāva huṃ*. This is the seal of the vast and non-empty maṇi universal offering (*mahā-amogha-maṇi-sarvapūjā-mudrā*). Join the two hands in the vajra-palms gesture.
Form the shape of a jewel by pinching and contracting the two index fingers;
it is completed by holding both thumbs upright.
Recite the Amoghamani-pūjā-mantra as follows:
Oṃ amoghapūjāmaṇipadmanarteśvara-samantaprasara hūṃ caturguru.
Place the left fist at the left hip.
Then recite the Vajra mantra three times.
Rotate the vajra three times to the left and three times to the right.
Offer it three times upward.
Perform the empowerment (adhiṣṭhāna) at five locations.
Place it upon the right breast.
Next, holding the bell in the left hand,
recite the mantra three times and shake it upward five times.
Twice shake upward between the left ears.
Next, pause and shake upward twice.
Then, rotate the pestle three times to the left and right respectively.
Consecrate the five places.
Place the vajra and bell together at their respective locations.
The mantra for the vajra is as follows:
Oṃ vajra-pāṇi hūṃ. The mantra for the bell is: Oṃ vajra-kaṇṭha tuṣya hūṃ.

Next, offer the argha with the mudrā and mantra as usual. Next, perform the binding of the four directions of Ākāśagarbha as usual. Next, the Vajraprākāra as usual. Next, the purification mantra as usual. These five [sections] of the Ākāśagarbha-vidhi were [transmitted] at Ninnaji and Kaimei-ji.

This transcription was completed at the Dharma Drum Terrace on Mount Mǔwěi; it was set down by the lamp on the fourth night of the eighth month of autumn in the second year of the Tiānmíng era, the *rényīn* year.
The *Kakuzenshō* states:
"The single fascicle of the *Shikyo* may be examined for its authenticity or spuriousness.
At Chijaku-in, Tōshū Jinin, on the second day of the eighth month of the first year of the Jōwa era, the cyclical year being *Jin-yu* (1351)."
Since Chijaku’s master, Jion, originally commissioned this transcription, I have now collated, corrected, and added punctuation points for its publication.

Recorded by Kaidō of Sōji-in, Chōkō-ji, on Mount Hōon, on the final day of the third month in the year of Kiei (the third year of Kyōwa), the day of Kōshi, the tenth day of the sexagenary cycle. Completed with one round of proofreading and annotations. Jishun.
